$comment: Elder Ina, by the Hearth gate. Gives the main quest and opens the gate.
speaker: Elder Ina

hello.text: A courier, in this weather? Let me guess. A crate of lamp-stones, and not one of them will light.

hello2.text: They won't, dear. Nothing will. The Hearth under this hill went out a month ago, and every wisp in the islands was born in that fire.

again.text: Back again, {player}? The Hearth's no warmer.

ask.text: What do you want to know?

what.text: Nobody knows. One morning the wisps came out grey and slow, and by the evening there were none. Then the halls below filled with ash-bound bones.

what2.text: Bones held together by cold ash. They don't hate anyone. They just... won't let the fire be tended.

who.text: I do, with a key, a broom and too many stairs. And the Cinder Warden did, long before me: an old guardian built to keep the Hearth. It hasn't let anyone past since the fire died.

help.text: You've a sword, a shield and you're not afraid of an old woman with a key. That's more than the rest of Cinder Cove. Will you go down?

notyet.text: Sensible. The gate will be here. So will I. So will the cold, unfortunately.

go.text: Then the gate is open. Buy a few tonics from Bram at the forge first, and rest by the hearthstones down there: they remember who's passed.

go2.text: And {player}: the Warden isn't wicked. It's doing its job very, very badly. Bring back whatever's left of the fire.

waiting.text: The gate's open. Down the steps, through the halls, and mind the bones. Tonics from Bram, rest at the hearthstones.

ember.text: You're carrying light, {player}. I can see it through your fingers. The Hearth is at the very bottom, past the Warden's chamber. Set the ember in it.

after.text: Listen. You can hear them, can't you? Wisps, humming in the chimney. Thank you, courier. Your crate's lit, by the way. Every stone.
